div.p: The Customer Risk Assessment (CRA) constitutes an automated, bot-driven evaluation framework designed to assess each customer's exposure to Money Laundering (ML), Terrorist Financing (TF), and Proliferation Financing (PF) risks.

The fundamental purpose of this methodology is to establish a data-driven, automated, and fully auditable framework that ensures strict adherence to Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations, Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) industry standards, and applicable local regulatory requirements.

p.strong: The CRA outcomes serve multiple critical organizational functions:

ul.li: Automated Customer Risk Identification: Bot-driven systematic identification and measurement of risk exposures across seven comprehensive customer risk factors
Control Enhancement and Resource Optimization: Inform strategic decisions regarding customer-specific control framework improvements
Governance and Oversight Support: Provide senior management and the Board with comprehensive, actionable intelligence

div.p: The CRA framework employs a sophisticated seven-factor customer risk assessment model that systematically evaluates risk exposure through comprehensive analysis of customer characteristics and behaviors.

ul.li: Customer Type (15% Weight) – Individual vs. Legal Entity risk assessment
Residency Status (10% Weight) – Resident vs. Non-Resident classification
Country Risk (15% Weight) – Geographic jurisdiction risk evaluation
Registration Type (10% Weight) – Mainland, Free Zone, or Offshore registration
Ownership Structure (10% Weight) – Transparent vs. Complex ownership analysis
Business Sector (10% Weight) – Industry and business activity risk profiling
PEP Exposure (30% Weight) – Politically Exposed Person status and exposure

div.p: Risk Rating Scale: 1 = Low Risk, 2 = Medium Risk, 3 = High Risk

The CRA framework incorporates rigorous data quality controls to ensure assessment accuracy and reliability. All critical data elements utilized in risk scoring calculations are designated as mandatory fields.

p.strong: The following fields constitute mandatory data requirements:

ul.li: Customer classification (individual or corporate entity)
Residency jurisdiction and nationality information
Country of incorporation and Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) nationalities
Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status and sanctions screening results
Customer onboarding and service delivery channel
Associated product(s) and service(s) relationships

p.strong: This comprehensive data governance approach delivers:

ul.li: Complete Data Coverage: 100% data completeness across all CRA assessment inputs
Computational Accuracy: Precise calculation of risk scores through verified data sets
Regulatory Defensibility: Comprehensive documentation and full audit traceability

div.p: The CRA methodology employs an automated, bot-driven assessment process designed to ensure systematic and comprehensive risk evaluation.

ol.li: Automated Rule Engine – Bot CRA automatically evaluates all seven customer risk factors using configurable business rules
Weighted Score Calculation – Each factor score is multiplied by its weight and aggregated
Policy Override Application – System applies policy overrides (e.g., foreign PEP minimum high risk)
Real-time Risk Determination – Final risk rating is automatically calculated and updated

ul.li: Enhanced Customer Risk Rule – Primary rule evaluating all seven customer factors with proper weighting
Enhanced Product Risk Rule – Evaluates product/service risk levels with user-configurable scoring
Enhanced Geography Risk Rule – CRR integration with country risk ratings and FATF compliance status
Enhanced Channel Risk Rule – Comprehensive onboarding channel risk assessment
PEP Check Rule – Automated PEP screening and risk evaluation
CRA Scenarios Rule – Handles regulatory, reputational, and override scenarios

div.p: The Bot CRA system automatically calculates customer risk scores through weighted evaluation of seven distinct risk factors.

ul.li: Customer Type: Individual (Score: 1), Legal Entity (Score: 3)
Residency Status: Resident (Score: 1), Non-Resident (Score: 3)
Country Risk: Low-risk (1), Medium-risk (2), High-risk (3) jurisdictions with CRR integration
Registration Type: Mainland (1), Free Zone (2), Offshore (3)
Ownership Structure: Transparent (1), Complex/Opaque (3)
Business Sector: Low-risk (1), Medium-risk (2), High-risk (3) sectors
PEP Exposure: No PEP (1), Domestic PEP/RCA (2), Foreign/International PEP (3)

p.style: margin-bottom: 0.5rem; color: #4b5563; font-family: monospace; background: #f3f4f6; padding: 0.5rem; border-radius: 4px;

ul.li: Low Risk: Score < 1.7
Medium Risk: Score 1.7 - 2.4
High Risk: Score ≥ 2.4

div.p: The Bot CRA system includes automated policy overrides that ensure minimum risk levels for specific high-risk scenarios:

ul.li: When foreign PEP is identified, system automatically assigns minimum High risk rating (Score: 2.4)
Applies regardless of calculated score from other factors
Ensures regulatory compliance for PEP risk management
Customers with expired KYC documentation automatically receive minimum High risk rating
Ensures timely KYC renewal and compliance with regulatory requirements
Sanctions Screening Results: Direct integration with screening outcomes
Case Management Integration: Real-time updates based on case resolutions
Multi-layer UBO Screening: Extends sanctions checks through ownership chains (up to 5 levels)

div.p: The Bot CRA outputs serve as critical inputs for the Enterprise-Wide Risk Assessment (EWRA) framework:

ul.li: Customer Pillar: CRA results directly feed into the Customer risk pillar in EWRA
Weighted Contribution: Customer risk represents 40% of overall EWRA calculation
Real-time Updates: CRA changes automatically reflect in EWRA calculations

ol.li: Customer Risk (40%) – Bot CRA outputs and customer risk distribution
Product Risk (25%) – Product and service risk assessment
Geography Risk (20%) – Geographic and jurisdictional risk analysis
Channel Risk (15%) – Onboarding and delivery channel risk evaluation

ul.li: Automated Evaluation: Eliminates manual bias and ensures consistent application of risk criteria
Real-time Processing: Immediate risk assessment as customer data is updated
Rule-based Logic: Transparent, auditable decision-making process
Scalable Solution: Handles large customer volumes without human intervention
Customer Database: Real-time access to customer profiles and relationships
Sanctions Screening: Integration with global sanctions databases and screening results
PEP Databases: Access to Politically Exposed Person information
Country Risk Data: CRR ratings and FATF compliance status integration
Case Management: Real-time updates from investigative processes
Full Audit Trail: Complete logging of all risk assessment decisions and factor scores
Rule Transparency: Clear documentation of scoring logic and business rules
Regulatory Alignment: Designed to meet FATF, CAMS, and local regulatory requirements
Policy Enforcement: Automated application of organizational risk policies

div.p: The Bot CRA methodology represents a significant advancement in automated customer risk assessment, providing:

ul.li: Comprehensive 7-factor risk evaluation with proper weighting and scoring
Automated, consistent decision-making through rule-based evaluation
Real-time risk assessment with immediate updates and alerts
Full regulatory compliance through policy enforcement and audit trails
Enterprise integration with EWRA and other risk management systems
Scalable, efficient processing of large customer volumes

div.p: This automated approach ensures consistent, objective, and auditable customer risk assessments while maintaining the flexibility to adapt to changing regulatory requirements and business needs.

Actions: Choose to either elevate customer to high risk or block customer entirely.
